scenes.tts: In a mouse, the brain's own immune cells were not made by the brain. So where were they made?
scenes.visual: Title card: One Job, Three Birthplaces. A mouse brain with small branched microglia glowing gold; a question mark beside it.
scenes.narration: In a mouse, the brain's own immune cells were not made by the brain. So where were they made?

scenes.tts: They are called microglia. In mice, most of them descend from cells born in the yolk sac, a membrane outside the embryo.
scenes.visual: A mouse embryo at about E9.5 with the yolk sac outside it, coloured gold. Gold cells drift from the yolk sac toward the head.
scenes.narration: They are called microglia. In mice, most of them descend from cells born in the yolk sac, a membrane outside the embryo.

scenes.tts: Glia, the non-neuronal cells among neurons, do not share one birthplace.
scenes.visual: A field of neurons with glia between them, all grey at first.
scenes.narration: Glia, the non-neuronal cells among neurons, do not share one birthplace.

scenes.tts: Astrocytes, oligodendrocytes and ependymal cells come from the neural tube. Most come through the same pool of radial glia that made the neurons.
scenes.visual: The neural tube wall lights sage. Radial glia span it; a neuron buds off, then an astrocyte. Astrocyte, oligodendrocyte and ependymal icons turn sage.
scenes.narration: Astrocytes, oligodendrocytes and ependymal cells come from the neural tube. Most come through the same pool of radial glia that made the neurons.

scenes.tts: Microglia, in mice, come from the yolk sac. Schwann cells and satellite glia come from the neural crest.
scenes.visual: Microglia icon turns gold, linked to the yolk sac. Crest streams leave the dorsal edge of the tube in clay; Schwann and satellite glia icons turn clay.
scenes.narration: Microglia, in mice, come from the yolk sac. Schwann cells and satellite glia come from the neural crest.

scenes.tts: Now take two cells with the same job.
scenes.visual: Three labels: neural tube (sage), yolk sac (gold), neural crest (clay).
scenes.narration: Now take two cells with the same job.

scenes.tts: Oligodendrocytes wrap central axons in myelin. Myelinating Schwann cells wrap peripheral axons in myelin.
scenes.visual: Split screen: a sage oligodendrocyte wrapping an axon in the spinal cord; a clay Schwann cell wrapping an axon in a nerve. Label: same job.
scenes.narration: Oligodendrocytes wrap central axons in myelin. Myelinating Schwann cells wrap peripheral axons in myelin.

scenes.tts: Mice lacking the genes Olig one and Olig two have no spinal cord oligodendrocytes. Should they lose the Schwann cells of their nerves too?
scenes.caption: Mice lacking the genes Olig1 and Olig2 have no spinal cord oligodendrocytes. Should they lose the Schwann cells of their nerves too?
scenes.visual: On screen: Olig1 and Olig2 removed. Spinal cord oligodendrocytes gone. Nerve Schwann cells too? Pause and predict.
scenes.narration: Mice lacking the genes Olig1 and Olig2 have no spinal cord oligodendrocytes. Should they lose the Schwann cells of their nerves too?

scenes.tts: No, not as a lineage. Schwann cells come from neural crest outside the cord, so they do not need Olig genes themselves.
scenes.visual: Row 1: Olig1 and Olig2 removed. Sage oligodendrocytes vanish from the cord; the clay Schwann cell lineage along the nerve stays. Small note: root Schwann cells also need motor axons.
scenes.narration: No, not as a lineage. Schwann cells come from neural crest outside the cord, so they do not need Olig genes themselves.

scenes.tts: These mice also lack spinal motor neurons, made by the same strip of cord.
scenes.visual: The ventral strip of the cord, pMN, in Olig2 colour; motor neurons fade with the oligodendrocytes. Label: same birthplace, lost together.
scenes.narration: These mice also lack spinal motor neurons, made by the same strip of cord.

scenes.tts: The reverse holds too. Remove the receptor Erb B three, and nerves lose their Schwann cell precursors. Oligodendrocytes do not need it.
scenes.caption: The reverse holds too. Remove the receptor ErbB3, and nerves lose their Schwann cell precursors. Oligodendrocytes do not need it.
scenes.visual: Row 2: ErbB3 removed. The nerve empties of clay precursors; a sage oligodendrocyte lacking ErbB3 still develops normally.
scenes.narration: The reverse holds too. Remove the receptor ErbB3, and nerves lose their Schwann cell precursors. Oligodendrocytes do not need it.

scenes.tts: Same job, different early requirements in these two examples.
scenes.visual: Two rows side by side; the word 'job' fades, the birthplace colours stay. Label: same job, different early requirements.
scenes.narration: Same job, different early requirements in these two examples.

scenes.tts: But a different birthplace does not guarantee different genes. Sox ten is needed by both lineages, at different stages.
scenes.caption: But a different birthplace does not guarantee different genes. Sox10 is needed by both lineages, at different stages.
scenes.visual: Sox10 card: arrows to both the sage oligodendrocyte and the clay Schwann cell, each at its own stage. Label: some genes are shared.
scenes.narration: But a different birthplace does not guarantee different genes. Sox10 is needed by both lineages, at different stages.

scenes.tts: So here is the idea to carry. Glia is a job, not a lineage.
scenes.visual: Rule card, line 1: Glia is a job, not a lineage.
scenes.narration: So here is the idea to carry. Glia is a job, not a lineage.

scenes.tts: To predict which glia a gene removes, ask where the cell was born.
scenes.visual: Rule card, line 2: Ask where the cell was born.
scenes.narration: To predict which glia a gene removes, ask where the cell was born.

scenes.tts: Then ask what its progenitor needed from that gene, at that time. What the cell does is a weaker guide.
scenes.visual: Rule card, line 3: and what its progenitor needed from that gene, then. What the cell does: a weaker guide.
scenes.narration: Then ask what its progenitor needed from that gene, at that time. What the cell does is a weaker guide.

scenes.tts: The rule predicts the first deficit, not the final count after the animal compensates.
scenes.visual: Scope note: predicts the first deficit; not the final count after compensation.
scenes.narration: The rule predicts the first deficit, not the final count after the animal compensates.

scenes.tts: Next question. How do you find out where a cell was born?
scenes.visual: Closing card: Next, how do you trace a birthplace? A stained cell beside a question mark.
scenes.narration: Next question. How do you find out where a cell was born?
